title.narrative: Stabilisation and People-Centred Security Reforms in Syria

description.narrative:
The DCAF proposal, titled "Stabilisation and People-Centred Security Reforms in Syria", outlines an 18-month, EU-funded initiative aimed at strengthening inclusive, accountable, and effective security sector governance in post-conflict Syria following the collapse of the Assad regime in December 2024.

The project adopts a dual-track approach, combining (i) national-level institutional reforms¿such as supporting the Ministry of Interior in developing a SSG/R roadmap, improving legal frameworks, and enhancing weapons and ammunition management (WAM)¿with (ii) local-level community engagement through the establishment of Community Safety Councils (CSCs) in six governorates (Homs, Aleppo, Latakia, Deir ez-Zor, Al-Hasakah, and As-Suwayda). These CSCs will serve as platforms for dialogue between communities (including women, youth, and marginalised groups) and security actors to rebuild trust and address local security needs.

The project builds on DCAF¿s prior scoping and inception phases (2025¿2026), leverages partnerships with Syrian civil society (e.g., GLOCA, Bidayatuna) and technical partners like the Small Arms Survey, and aligns with broader EU stabilisation priorities. Sustainability is ensured through local ownership, institutional anchoring, and adaptive implementation, with expected outcomes including improved rule of law, accountability, and inclusive security governance, measured via indicators like the World Bank¿s Worldwide Governance Indicators (WGI).
